trajectory: disitamab vedotin / RC48 / Aidixi / RemeGen + Seagen/Pfizer
refined_summary: Search discovery materially sharpens two blind-memory uncertainties. RemeGen's 2021 license agreement with Seagen was executed on 2021-08-08 and became effective on 2021-09-15; Seagen received exclusive development/commercialization rights in all countries outside the RemeGen Territory, while RemeGen retained Asia excluding Japan and Singapore. RemeGen states that China approved disitamab vedotin for HER2-overexpressing locally advanced/metastatic gastric cancer on 2021-06-09 and that the urothelial-cancer indication was approved on 2021-12-31. A 2025 RemeGen annual report still described Pfizer/Seagen as conducting global trials, so the rights trajectory should not be assumed to have reverted merely because Pfizer acquired Seagen.

blind_memory_discrepancies.blind_fragment: Seagen regional license recalled approximately as ex-Asia or ex-Greater-China-style
blind_memory_discrepancies.post_seal_refinement: Contract defines RemeGen Territory as Asia excluding Japan and Singapore; Seagen territory is the rest of world, so Japan and Singapore belong on the Seagen side.

blind_memory_discrepancies.blind_fragment: China urothelial approval remembered only as an approximate 2021-2022 event
blind_memory_discrepancies.post_seal_refinement: RemeGen later states NMPA marketing approval occurred on 2021-12-31.
